name: browser-connector
description: Attach your own everyday browser to a PersonalClaw you already run, so a browse task with target 'user_browser' can act inside a session you are already logged into. The connector is a browser extension that pairs with the gateway using the SAME device-session machinery your phone does, then announces — over loopback only — the CDP page-target endpoint your browser exposes, which is exactly what the gateway's connector seam consumes. It speaks a deliberately narrow, closed contract: navigate, read-outline, click, type, close, and nothing else. It opens no listening surface of its own: every call is an outbound loopback request, and the extension's host permissions are loopback-only by manifest, so it literally cannot reach anywhere else. It never reads, stores, or types into a password field. The per-task grant, the task-named tab group, and close-to-kill land next; this bundle establishes the connection and the contract.
author: PersonalClaw

clientInstall.shell: set -e; DEST="$HOME/.personalclaw/apps/browser-connector"; git clone --depth 1 --filter=blob:none --sparse https://github.com/PersonalClaw/PersonalClawApps "$DEST"; git -C "$DEST" sparse-checkout set browser-connector; echo "Unpacked extension: $DEST/browser-connector/extension"
clientInstall.postInstall: echo 'Load the unpacked extension at ~/.personalclaw/apps/browser-connector/browser-connector/extension in your browser (developer mode), start the browser with a loopback --remote-debugging-port, then pair it from Settings -> Devices.'
